subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
lesson: Lesson 7: English in action – Giving advice
outcomes: Understand a dialogue where a teacher gives advice.
Give advice with phrases like I think you should… and Why don’t you…?
Hear and say silent letters in words like shouldn’t and lightning.

tf.s: Eliza wants to help animals that are in danger.
tf.why: Yes, and Miss Brown gives her advice.

tf.s: Miss Brown tells Eliza to look online to find out more.
tf.why: Right! Looking online is one of her ideas.

tf.s: Miss Brown tells Eliza to put a notice in the school newsletter.
tf.why: Correct! A notice tells other students.

tf.s: We say “If I was you, I would…” in the lesson phrase.
tf.why: The phrase is If I were you, I would…

tf.s: “Why don’t you…?” is a way to give advice.
tf.why: Great! Why don’t you buy a book? is advice.

tf.s: The letter l is silent in “shouldn’t”.
tf.why: Yes, we don’t say the l in shouldn’t.

tf.s: In “lightning”, we say the letters gh clearly.
tf.why: The gh in lightning is silent.

tf.s: We say “Perhaps you ought learn some vocabulary.”
tf.why: We say ought to: Perhaps you ought to learn some vocabulary.

tf.s: “You could always…” is a phrase for complaining.
tf.why: You could always… is a phrase for giving advice.

tf.s: Miss Brown says Eliza should make the garden dangerous for animals.
tf.why: She says Eliza can make the garden safe for animals.

boxes.q: ___ don’t you look for one online?
If I ___ you, I would have a look at your garden.
boxes.why: We say If I were you.
You could always… gives a helpful idea.

boxes.q: Perhaps you ___ to ask your teacher for help.

boxes.why: The l in shouldn’t is not pronounced.

boxes.q: What is Miss Brown doing in the dialogue?
Advice for “I’m not doing well in Maths.”
o: Perhaps you ought to ask your teacher for help.
boxes.why: Asking the teacher is helpful advice.
I think you should… is an advice phrase.

boxes.q: Advice for someone who wants to recycle more:
o: You should recycle plastic and glass bottles.

hunt.q: Put a notice in the school…

mcq.q: What does Eliza want to do?
o: Help animals that are in danger
mcq.why: Eliza wants to help endangered animals.

mcq.q: Which is one piece of advice Miss Brown gives?
o: Look online to find out more.
Stay at home and do nothing.
mcq.why: Looking online helps Eliza find out what animals she can help.

mcq.q: Which is NOT a phrase for giving advice?
o: Excuse me, where is the bank?
If I were you, I would…
mcq.why: Asking for directions is not giving advice.

mcq.q: Your friend says: “I don’t know what present to get my mother for Eid.” Choose the best advice.
o: If I were you, I would buy her some flowers.
If I was you, I buy flowers.
mcq.why: This uses the advice phrase correctly.

mcq.q: Your friend has an English test tomorrow. Which advice is correct?
o: Perhaps you ought to learn some vocabulary.
Perhaps you ought learn some vocabulary.
Perhaps you to ought learn vocabulary.

mcq.q: Complete: A: “I want to buy a present.” B: “___ buy a book?”
Why is putting a notice in the school newsletter good advice for Eliza?
o: Many students will read it and can help too.
It is a way to buy animals.
It stops climate change by itself.
mcq.why: A notice tells other students about her idea.

mcq.q: Which word has a silent letter?
mcq.why: The l in shouldn’t is silent.

mcq.q: Which reply gives advice, not an order?
o: You could always ask your teacher.
mcq.why: You could always… is a soft way to give advice.
